AUDIT: FAIL
Objective Understood: Reviewed worker task 'sweep-adopt-veridian-scripts-204-test-first-real-batch-of-load-bearing-sc' (risk tier: tier1) by reading the actual diff, not a self-report.
Standards Reviewed: AGENTS.md Operating Rule 7c structured audit protocol; risk-tier.py's deterministic tier classification.
Scope Confirmed:  PLATFORM_COMPLETION_CHECKLIST.json                 | 232 ++++++++++------
 PLATFORM_COMPLETION_CHECKLIST.md                   |  66 ++---
 test_gtm_write_category_result.py                  | 200 ++++++++++++++
 test_metadata_reconciliation.py                    | 147 ++++++++++
 test_owner_status.py                               | 142 ++++++++++
 test_recover_failed_workers.py                     | 151 ++++++++++
 test_resource_governor_tick_loop.py                | 114 ++++++++
 test_supervisor_sweep.py                           | 118 ++++++++
 ...r_entrypoint_and_docworker_entrypoint_guards.py | 303 +++++++++++++++++++++
 9 files changed, 1359 insertions(+), 114 deletions(-)
Evidence Recorded: This diff adds 7 new test files covering previously-untested load-bearing scripts (gtm_write_category_result.py, metadata_reconciliation.py, owner_status.py, recover-failed-workers.py, resource_governor_tick_loop.sh, supervisor-sweep.sh, worker-entrypoint.sh/doc-worker-entrypoint.sh) plus a regenerated PLATFORM_COMPLETION_CHECKLIST.json/.md; it is purely additive (no .github/workflows/** changes, no production script logic touched) and 6 of the 7 test files are genuinely meaningful -- they exec the real scripts/bash blocks against real temp SQLite DBs with real schema and assert on real output, not mocked-out rubber-stamping. However, actually running pytest on the new files today (rather than trusting the checklist's embedded 'pytest_summary: 588 passed' self-report) reproduces a real failure: test_owner_status.py::test_hours_filter_excludes_old_rows hardcodes an absolute wall-clock timestamp fixture that has aged past the script's rolling '--hours 48' window since the tests were authored, so the suite as submitted does not currently pass. Per the standing quality-gate rule (evidence must reflect the actual diff, not a self-report, and quality gates must already be passing), this fails the bar for autonomous tier1 merge right now even though the fix is small and well-scoped for a targeted follow-up. Issues found: test_owner_status.py::test_hours_filter_excludes_old_rows hardcodes an absolute timestamp ('2026-08-06T00:00:00Z') as a 'recent' row and asserts it survives a --hours 48 filter against owner_status.py's real datetime('now', '-48 hours') query; verified by actually running pytest today (2026-08-16) that this test now FAILS, contradicting the diff's own checklist claim of tests_pass: true / 'pytest_summary: 588 passed' for owner_status.py -- needs a relative timestamp (e.g. now - 1h) instead of a fixed date before this can be trusted as passing evidence.; Minor: test_owner_status.py calls __import__('tempfile').mkstemp()[1] and discards the returned file descriptor without closing it (harmless fd leak in a test process, but sloppy).
Severity Classified: medium
Verdict: fail
Corrective Action Owner: Worker to address the findings listed above and resubmit.
Re-Audit Scheduled: Required after corrective changes are pushed.
